title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) in Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy

sections.title: Indications for Vitrectomy in PDR
content: Non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage (lasting > 1-3 months).
Tractional retinal detachment (TRD) involving or threatening the macula.
Combined tractional/rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.
Progressive fibrovascular proliferation despite panretinal photocoagulation (PRP).
Dense premacular subhyaloid hemorrhage.
Iris neovascularization (NVI) or neovascular glaucoma with media opacity.

sections.title: Surgical Step-by-Step: The Core Procedure
content: Step 1: Port placement (usually 3.5-4.0mm from the limbus).
Step 2: Core vitrectomy to clear central hemorrhage.
Step 3: Posterior hyaloid separation (often using triamcinolone for visualization).
Step 4: Membrane delamination vs. segmentation using vertical scissors or pick.
Step 5: Endolaser photocoagulation (the 'new' PRP).
Step 6: Fluid-air/gas exchange or silicone oil tamponade if indicated.

sections.title: Red Flags: Intraoperative Risk Factors
content: Iatrogenic retinal breaks due to over-zealous membrane peeling.
Uncontrolled hemorrhage from fibrovascular stalks.
Unrecognized choroidal effusion.
Damage to the crystalline lens (cataractogenesis).

content.explanation: P: Peripheral clear (vitreous removal), R: Release traction (membrane peeling), E: Endolaser (ablation of ischemic retina), P: Pressure/Tamponade (gas/oil).

sections.title: Preoperative Workup Checklist
content: B-Scan Ultrasonography (to rule out RD).
Gonioscopy (check for NVI/NVA).
OCT (assess macular involvement).
HbA1c optimization (perioperative glycemic control).
Anti-VEGF injection 3-5 days pre-op (to induce regression of neovascularization).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: The use of anti-VEGF prior to surgery significantly decreases intraoperative bleeding but may worsen pre-existing TRD through 'contraction effect'.
Internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling is often required if macular edema persists.
Always check the status of the lens; combine vitrectomy with phacoemulsification if cataract is significant, especially in older patients.
Endolaser should reach the ora serrata to ensure maximum ablation of ischemic retina.
